claims.statement: The MCP server's MediaWiki access is a process-wide singleton: src/common/nodemwBot.ts holds botInstance, serverConfig, authenticated, mediaWikiVersion and namespaceCache as module-scope state, and both the bootstrap in src/index.ts and tool handlers (including the read-before-write guard in pageState.ts) resolve the client through getBot() at call time rather than receiving an injected instance.

getBot() throws the error 'Bot not initialized. Server must be started first.' when botInstance is null, so tool handlers are only safe because bootstrap exits the process on any failure before the stdio transport connects.

initBot() constructs the bot from config and performs a login only when both username and password are set; login is wrapped in a hand-written Promise (not promisifyBotMethod) that sets authenticated = true on success and rejects with 'Login failed for user <name>: <message>' so the failing account is identifiable.

The authenticated flag is a startup snapshot: it is set only inside the successful-login callback, is never reset to false by initBot (so re-initialising without credentials leaves a previously true value), and is consumed by src/index.ts both to fetch whoami data and to decide whether write tools are registered at all, meaning tools do not re-check authentication per call.

autoDetectPath() discovers the API script path by trying the candidates ['/w', ''] in that fixed order, building a throwaway Bot per candidate and calling getSiteInfo(['general']) through promisifyBotMethod, returning the first path that answers and otherwise throwing an error naming both attempted URLs and asking for an explicit --path.

Auto-detection probes are anonymous even when credentials are configured, because createBotFromConfig forwards username/password only into the nodemw constructor while logIn is invoked exclusively by initBot; probe bots are never assigned to botInstance, so their sessions and internal caches are discarded.

The MediaWiki version is cached outside the bot object: setMediaWikiVersion stores a string, getMediaWikiVersion parses /^(\d+)\.(\d+)/ into a major+minor float (or returns null when unset or unparsable), and bootstrap populates it once via promisifyBotMethod while tolerating both a bare string and a { version } response shape and swallowing all failures as non-fatal.

Four write tools use the cached MediaWiki version to choose a token type, requesting 'csrf' when the version is at least 1.24 and falling back to the action-specific 'block', 'protect', 'unblock'/'block', or 'undelete' token otherwise, so a null or truncated version silently selects the legacy token path.

clearBotCache() resets botInstance to null and authenticated to false but deliberately or accidentally leaves mediaWikiVersion intact, so a reset followed by re-initialisation against a different wiki would still report the previous wiki's version; the function has no callers anywhere in src, making it an unused reset hook.

Two callback-to-Promise helpers cover nodemw: promisifyBotMethod appends a Node-style (err, result) callback and dispatches dynamically via (bot as any)[method], so it fits only single-result methods, while callApi in src/common/utils.ts wraps the four-argument api.call (err, info, next, data) and resolves the raw data object so query/continue topology survives; calls whose callbacks deliver an extra value — getToken(title, type, cb) and getArticle(title, followRedirect, cb) with redirect info — are still hand-wrapped in new Promise.

promisifyBotMethod is defined twice: src/common/utils.ts carries a semantically identical copy that no module imports, because every tool module, src/index.ts and pageState.ts import it from nodemwBot.js. Edits to the utils.ts copy therefore have no runtime effect, and utils.ts depends on the nodemw Bot type for its live callApi helper rather than for that dead copy.

createBotFromConfig forwards server, path, protocol (defaulting to https), port, proxy, concurrency, debug, username, password, domain, and dryRun (behind an @ts-expect-error because nodemw's published BotOptions omits it), coerces empty-string credentials to undefined, and resolves the User-Agent from userAgent plus userAgentAppend, which is consumed rather than forwarded to nodemw.

DEFAULT_USER_AGENT, assembled in src/server.ts from the nodemw version, Node version, platform/arch, this package's name and version, and the MCP SDK version, is both the fallback User-Agent and the prefix used when userAgentAppend is enabled, making it the single place that identifies the client to wiki operators.

The ServerConfig token field is inert: it is declared on the interface and read from --token in parseCliArgs, but createBotFromConfig neither destructures nor forwards it and login is gated only on username and password, so supplying a token yields a silent anonymous read-only session even though the README documents --token and NODEMW_MCP_MW_TOKEN as alternatives to credentials (the environment variable is never read at all).

initServerConfig stores the ServerConfig in a module variable reached only through getServerConfig(), and nothing under src/ calls that getter (only the test fake declares it), so the bootstrap call is a write-only placeholder for a config-owner role rather than an active configuration source.

The CLI parser never populates proxy, concurrency, or domain, so those ServerConfig fields are only reachable by calling initBot programmatically; the shipped binary configures just the parsed flags and environment variables.

An explicitly empty API path cannot be forced from the CLI: pathExplicit is computed with !!(values.path ?? values.endpoint ?? pathFromEnv) so '--path ""' is falsy and re-triggers auto-detection, contradicting the auto-detection error message that recommends --path "" for root installs.

The second block of process-wide state is owned by pageState.ts: readState is a Map keyed by pageid holding a ReadRecord (revid, revTimestamp, readAt) and writeCache is keyed by title holding pageid plus the revid written this session. markAsRead, recordReadFromApi and markAsWritten write them; isRead only tests key presence, conflictGuardParams derives starttimestamp/basetimestamp, and findStaleWrite is the only consumer that compares the stored revid with the current one. clearReadState is called only by tests and clearBotCache touches neither map, so both persist for the life of the process and survive a bot reset.

src/common/nodemwBot.ts imports DEFAULT_USER_AGENT from ../server.js, inverting the usual layering so the runtime depends on the server-factory module and src/server.ts remains the only place where the default User-Agent string can be changed.

User-Agent resolution has exactly three branches: DEFAULT_USER_AGENT plus the custom string when both userAgent and userAgentAppend are set, the custom string alone when only userAgent is set, and DEFAULT_USER_AGENT otherwise — so passing --user-agent-append without -A is a silent no-op rather than a warning.

Startup splits into a fatal phase and a tolerant phase: CLI parsing, API path auto-detection, bot construction plus optional login, and the siteinfo/site-statistics fetch each print an error and call process.exit(1) on failure, whereas the MediaWiki version probe and the authenticated whoami lookup run inside swallow-all catches, so the process still reaches registerAllTools(server, auth) even when the version cache stays null.

startLoginHeartbeat polls meta=userinfo every 60 seconds through fetchWhoami and downgrades the session only on positive anonymous evidence: isWhoamiAuthenticated requires userinfo.id above 0 and no anon flag, authenticated is set to false before onDisconnect fires so the callback runs at most once, network and API errors are swallowed by an empty catch, and the interval is unref'd so it never keeps the process alive. Bootstrap arms it only for sessions that started authenticated, and because isAuthenticated() is read only while building the startup description and tool surface, the downgrade withdraws no already-registered tool — the one observable effect is a single LOGIN SESSION EXPIRED banner on stderr.

A namespace cache maps lowercased namespace names — localized, canonical and siprop=namespacealiases aliases — to numeric ids, is populated once at bootstrap from the getSiteInfo call that also fetches general and languages, skips negative pseudo-namespaces such as Special and Media, and is read through lookupNamespaceId, which returns null both when the cache was never filled and when the name is unknown so callers keep legacy behavior. clearBotCache does not clear it, and get-pages-by-prefix is its only consumer.

Nothing in the runtime is persisted: login cookies live in the Bot's cookie jar, read-before-write evidence in pageState's maps, and the version/namespace caches in module variables. Because an MCP client reconnect starts a brand-new process (as the generated instructions state), a reconnect loses the login session and the read evidence at once, so the agent must log in again or fall back to guest and re-read every page before writing.

Five consumers read the cached MediaWiki version: block, protect, unblock and undelete pick csrf at 1.24 or newer versus an action-specific legacy token, and diff-preview refuses to run below 1.24 and sends topst only when the version is null or at least 1.27 — so both a missing cache and a stale cache silently select legacy behavior instead of failing loudly.

clearBotCache resets only botInstance and authenticated; mediaWikiVersion, namespaceCache, the heartbeat interval and pageState's two maps all survive, so resetting and re-initialising against a different wiki inherits the previous wiki's version number and namespace table.

initBot assigns botInstance before attempting logIn, so a rejected login leaves the module holding a constructed but unauthenticated client: the CLI exits immediately, while an embedder sees getBot() succeed and isAuthenticated() stay false.

DEFAULT_USER_AGENT is assembled at module load in src/server.ts using createRequire to read the installed nodemw and MCP SDK package.json files, because both packages are esbuild externals resolved by npm on the installing machine, whereas this package's own version comes from a JSON import that the bundler inlines — so one UA string mixes runtime-resolved and build-time-pinned versions.

The runtime has an automated vitest suite (npm test runs vitest run) covering the namespace cache, pageState timestamps, errorResult annotations and an end-to-end MCP pass over every registered tool; but the tool tests replace the whole nodemwBot module with createNodemwBotMock, which stubs getBot, isAuthenticated, the heartbeat and the cache setters, so the singleton lifecycle, login path, authenticated state machine and both callback-to-Promise bridges are exercised by no test — namespaceCache.test.ts is the only test importing the real module.

test-server.js is a manual smoke script outside npm test: its only hard assertion is that dist/index.js exists, after which it spawns the binary without a target server, prints up to 500 characters of each stream, kills it after two seconds and reports completion regardless of the child's exit code, so it cannot fail on a broken startup beyond a missing build artifact.

On the pinned nodemw 0.26.0, api.call turns a top-level response error into a callback error whose message is 'Error returned by API: <info>', so callApi never resolves with an error key: the raw.error guards in its consumers are unreachable defensive code, and login-expiry versus edit-conflict can only be recognized by matching message text, which is what errorResult's LOGIN_EXPIRED_PATTERNS and EDIT_CONFLICT_PATTERNS do.
